Typographie, by Emil Ruder

The Basel school’s typography textbook, in three languages, with a cover built from blocks of letters.

Context

Typographie: Ein Gestaltungslehrbuch, 1967 (1st edition; 6th edition 1996). Offset, 28 × 22.3 cm, 220 pages. Published by Verlag Niggli AG, Sulgen; printed by Heer Druck AG. Photography by Werner Blaser, André Gürtler, and Armin Hofmann. eMuseum object 36839.

Ruder, born in Zürich in 1914, trained as a typesetter in Basel. The book was published in German, English, and French by Arthur Niggli in 1967. Wikipedia: Emil Ruder.

Ruder also designed covers of Typographische Monatsblätter, including the January 1961 issue devoted to Univers. Commons.

Observed

  • The square jacket is white with a large black field in which the letters of TYPOGRAPHIE appear white, each in its own black rectangle.
  • A very large T fills the right two thirds; Y fills a box above the smaller boxes; PO, GRA, and PHIE sit in a grid of small squares at lower left.
  • The small letters are mirrored, as if seen from the back of metal type.
  • Author and title appear once more in small plain type at top right, flush with the black field’s right edge.
  • There is no color: only black and white.

Why it belongs

The cover teaches the book’s lesson: one word divided into modules of different sizes, held by a grid. The mirrored letters point back to the composing room, where Ruder trained.

Borrow

Break one word into grid cells of unequal size to create hierarchy inside a single element.

Pair a very large display letter with a small, plain title line placed at an edge.
